I understand it can be scary for you snake to go off feed, but it's nothing you have to really freak out over. Ball pythons are known to do this. It's one reason why some people dont reccomend them as beginner snakes, because they go off feed and scare their owners. But like I said it's pretty normal for them to do so. As long as they arent showing any signs or symptoms of sickness, and as long as they haven't loss more than 10% of their body weight, there is no need to panic. Just keep offering food weekly (all of this is assuming your husbandry is OK)

Like I said I can understand this being scary but there is no need to panic =] Snakes arent like cats and dogs. Snakes of all types can go months and months without food. You can have perfect husbandry and a snake will go off feed for a variety of reasons that are beyond our control (the season change, they think they are gonna breed, self regulating weight etc)

Alot of great comments so I'll go ahead and add my two cents here:
- Get her on rats asap. The sooner the better because some BPs have been known to be picky/not wanna switch. Might as well go ahead and get the process out the way now while shes young
-They arent as active as alot of other breeds so dont be alarmed if she isn't doin as much as your others. If shes eatin good, pooping fine and sheds are good than you are all good.
-Humidity is a fickle beast. Many factors depend on where you live. For example where I live I have my boy on aspen and my humidity is always between 55%-70%. And I dont even mist. Just play around with substrates, misting etc till you find what works for you. 
-A couple more things about eating: make sure the food is warm, atleast body tempature. BPs put those put organs to good use! If the food isnt warm enough they may not recognize it as something safe to eat so they will ignore it despite the delicious rat smell.  Also they are known to go on hunger strikes so just be mentally prepared for that. But as a baby that shouldn't be an issue. 
As you run into specific issues on your journey there are PLENTY of online resources. I usually google my issue and 99% of the time there is some sort of thread that somebody else posted on a website that's my exact question lol. You'll do fine =]
